title: Devcontainer agent toolchain and hook wiring
summary: This change turns the devcontainer image from a Rust-only build box into a full agent factory: it pins and installs Node 22, pnpm, Bun, moon, gh, actionlint, uv, the four coding agents (codex, claude-code, opencode, omp), dsh from its own lockfile, the NVIDIA skill linters, and third-party skills, then wires every agent's hook files root-owned and read-only so `osf hook` runs on prompt and stop. It also replaces the system-wide `core.hooksPath` with a git wrapper that forces the hooks path only under the workspace mount, and adds build-time tests that prove the wrapper, the hooks, the toolchain read-only-ness and the image cleanliness.

lanes.subtitle: codex, claude-code, opencode, omp, dsh

nodes.label: Dockerfile
nodes.subtitle: .devcontainer/Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Pins every tool by version and SHA-256, installs the agents, builds the plugin workspace with pnpm, and runs the build-time test scripts.

nodes.label: Pinned tool downloads
nodes.subtitle: moon, gh, actionlint, uv, node, bun
nodes.summary: Each tool is fetched from its own release tarball and checked against a published SHA-256, with per-architecture selection from TARGETARCH.

nodes.label: Agent npm install
nodes.subtitle: codex, claude-code, opencode-ai, omp
nodes.summary: The four coding agents are installed as global npm packages into the root-owned Node install, then write bits are stripped.

nodes.label: dsh from lockfile
nodes.subtitle: .devcontainer/dsh
nodes.summary: dsh is installed with `npm ci` from its own committed package-lock.json, so its version is reproducible independently of the repo's pnpm workspace.

nodes.label: Plugin workspace build
nodes.subtitle: integrations/dsh, omp, opencode
nodes.summary: The three writing-check integrations are built from the repo's own pnpm lockfile so their dependency versions match what CI already tests.

nodes.label: Third-party skills
nodes.subtitle: archify, archify-review
nodes.summary: The skills CLI installs archify and archify-review at a pinned commit for opencode, codex and claude-code only; dsh and omp are not known to the skills tool.

nodes.label: Build-time tests
nodes.subtitle: git-wrapper, agent-hooks, toolchain-readonly, image-clean
nodes.summary: Each test script runs during the build and fails the image if the wrapper, the hook files, the read-only toolchain or the layer cleanliness is wrong.

nodes.label: devcontainer.json
nodes.subtitle: workspaceMount, remoteEnv
nodes.summary: Binds the repo at /workspace, forwards GH_TOKEN, and the postCreateCommand now checks osf, moon, node and pnpm.

nodes.label: git wrapper
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/git
nodes.summary: Refuses --no-verify and -n on commit and --no-verify on push, and forces core.hooksPath on the command line only for repositories under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT.

nodes.label: Root-owned git hooks
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/githooks
nodes.summary: pre-commit, commit-msg and pre-push, each only calling osf. The wrapper points git at them under the workspace.

nodes.label: osf-path.sh
nodes.subtitle: /etc/profile.d
nodes.summary: Restores PATH in login shells, which otherwise reset it before reading profile.d and drop osf, cargo and the agent binaries.

nodes.label: Agent hook files
nodes.subtitle: /etc/codex, /etc/claude-code, /etc/opencode, ~/.dsh, ~/.omp
nodes.summary: Each agent's hook config, written by `osf hooks install --agents` and then made root-owned and read-only, with system copies for codex, claude-code and opencode.

nodes.label: codex
nodes.subtitle: @openai/codex
nodes.summary: Reads /etc/codex/config.toml and /etc/codex/hooks; only the prompt event is wired because codex has no turn-end event.

nodes.label: claude-code
nodes.subtitle: @anthropic-ai/claude-code
nodes.summary: Reads ~/.claude/settings.json, mirrored to /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json so a changed HOME cannot move it.

nodes.label: opencode
nodes.subtitle: opencode-ai
nodes.summary: Reads ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, mirrored to /etc/opencode/opencode.json, and loads the osf-opencode-plugin from the home node_modules.

nodes.label: omp
nodes.subtitle: @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent
nodes.summary: Runs on Bun, not plain Node, and has no system-wide hook location, so its hook file stays under the home folder.

nodes.label: dsh
nodes.subtitle: @deepseek-ai/dsh
nodes.summary: Boots the factory and headless profiles, each carrying the osf-dsh-plugin and the Claude-format hooks bridge pointed at .claude/hooks.json.

nodes.label: osf hook
nodes.subtitle: prompt, stop
nodes.summary: Answers the agent hook events the image wires; it has no pre-tool-use event, so none is wired.

nodes.label: osf hooks install
nodes.subtitle: --agents --root
nodes.summary: Writes each agent's hook files from the [agents] table of osf.toml; the Dockerfile runs it and then locks the files down.

nodes.label: osf.toml [agents]
nodes.subtitle: agent table
nodes.summary: The one list of supported agents, their hook wiring and the default builder; every script reads it instead of naming an agent.

nodes.label: devcontainer_dockerfile.rs
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/tests
nodes.summary: The Rust test that asserts the Dockerfile's shape, updated for the new toolchain and hook blocks.

edges.label: osf hooks install
edges.summary: The build runs `osf hooks install --agents`, then chowns each written file root-owned and read-only, and mirrors the claude and opencode files to /etc.

edges.label: OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT=/workspace
edges.summary: devcontainer.json binds the repo at /workspace and the Dockerfile sets OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT to the same value, so the wrapper knows which repositories it governs.

edges.label: core.hooksPath
edges.summary: The wrapper passes core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks on the command line for every git call under the workspace, replacing the old system-wide setting.

edges.label: osf hook prompt|stop
edges.summary: Every wired hook file invokes `osf hook` for the prompt and stop events the CLI supports.

flows.title: Agent prompt reaches osf hook
flows.summary: A coding agent fires its prompt hook, the root-owned hook file runs `osf hook`, and the CLI answers the event.

flows.title: git commit under the workspace
flows.summary: A commit inside /workspace goes through the wrapper, which forces the hooks path, so the root-owned pre-commit and commit-msg hooks run and call osf.

views.summary: The running container: the git wrapper and hooks, the root-owned hook files, and the five agents that read them.
